record.original_question: For a preemptive multiprocessor real-time system under global scheduling, determine the computational complexity of feasibility analysis for sporadic task systems with arbitrary deadlines. The input is a sporadic task system tau and a positive integer m > 1; global scheduling permits a job to begin execution on any processor and to resume on any processor after preemption. Is tau feasible on a platform of m preemptive processors, meaning that for every legal sequence of job arrivals generated by tau there exists a schedule meeting all deadlines?

evidence.quote: In global scheduling, by contrast, a job may begin execution on any processor, and a preempted job may resume execution upon any processor.

Problem 3 (Multiprocessor global feasibility analysis – arbitrary-deadline tasks) Input: Sporadic task system τ . A positive integer m > 1. Question: Is τ feasible upon a platform comprised of m preemptive processors (under the global scheduling paradigm)?

For constrained-deadline and arbitrary-deadline systems, however, no algorithms – of any computational complexity whatsoever– are known; thus, the computational complexity of this problem remains wide open for such systems.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A sporadic task system is a finite collection τ = {τ_1, …, τ_n} of tasks, where each task τ_i = (C_i, D_i, T_i) is specified by a worst-case execution requirement C_i ∈ ℚ_{>0}, a (relative) deadline D_i ∈ ℚ_{>0}, and a minimum inter-arrival separation T_i ∈ ℚ_{>0}. No restriction is imposed between D_i and T_i (the "arbitrary-deadline" model). A legal job-arrival sequence generated by τ consists of, for each task τ_i, an arbitrary (possibly infinite) sequence of jobs whose successive release times differ by at least T_i; the job released at time r by τ_i has execution requirement C_i and absolute deadline r + D_i.

Given an integer m > 1, a platform of m identical preemptive processors is governed by the global scheduling paradigm: at every instant, any subset of at most m jobs may be executed in parallel (each on a distinct processor), and a preempted job may later resume execution on any processor (migration is allowed at no cost). A job is assumed to never execute on more than one processor simultaneously.

The task system τ is said to be feasible on m processors under global scheduling if, for every legal job-arrival sequence generated by τ, there exists a schedule on the m processors in which every job receives C_i units of execution between its release time and its absolute deadline.

Problem. Determine the computational complexity of deciding, given as input a sporadic task system τ with arbitrary deadlines and an integer m > 1, whether τ is feasible on m preemptive processors under global scheduling.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work after the problem was posed produced exact decision procedures for the arbitrary-deadline global feasibility problem (notably state-space / antichain algorithms by Baker–Cirinei and by Bonifaci–Marchetti-Spaccamela), and PSPACE-hardness has been established for related multiprocessor sporadic feasibility problems. However, a tight complexity classification (matching upper and lower bounds) specifically for arbitrary-deadline global feasibility on m identical preemptive processors does not appear to be settled in the literature, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Multiprocessor schedulability of arbitrary-deadline sporadic tasks: complexity and antichain algorithm
status_evidence.snippet: complexity and antichain algorithm for arbitrary-deadline sporadic tasks on multiprocessors
status_evidence.claim: Provides complexity results and an exact antichain-based algorithm for the global schedulability problem with arbitrary deadlines.

status_evidence.title: Feasibility Analysis of Sporadic Real-Time Multiprocessor Task Systems
status_evidence.snippet: first algorithm for testing feasibility of a system of sporadic real-time tasks on identical processors
status_evidence.claim: An algorithm for sporadic multiprocessor feasibility was developed addressing the open problem, though tight complexity is not fully pinned down.

status_evidence.title: A Survey of Hard Real-Time Scheduling for Multiprocessor Systems
status_evidence.claim: Survey discusses the state of feasibility/schedulability analyses for arbitrary-deadline sporadic systems under global scheduling.
